deals.name: Orion Network Systems
deals.description: Networking software maker folded into Apple's connectivity efforts.

deals.name: Network Innovations
deals.description: Apple's first acquisition — database-access software for connecting Macs to corporate data.

deals.name: Styleware
deals.description: Maker of AppleWorks GS productivity suite for the Apple IIGS.

deals.name: Coral Software
deals.description: Lisp-language developer; became Macintosh Common Lisp.

deals.name: NeXT Software, Inc.
deals.valueNote: ~$427M total consideration ($400M+ cash plus stock) per Apple's FY1997 10-K; announced Dec 20, 1996
deals.description: The deal that changed everything: NeXT's OPENSTEP became Mac OS X, and the acquisition returned Steve Jobs to Apple — first as advisor, then interim CEO by September 1997.
deals.appleLanguage: FY1997 10-K: the acquisition included a $375M charge for in-process research and development.
deals.source: Apple FY1997 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR); Apple press release Dec 20, 1996

deals.name: Power Computing (Mac OS license assets)
deals.description: Bought back the leading Mac clone maker's license and customer base, ending the clone program that was cannibalizing Mac sales.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple press release: 'Apple to acquire Power Computing's core assets' (Sep 2, 1997).

deals.name: Xemplar Education (stake sale)
deals.description: Sold Apple's stake in the UK education joint venture to Granada.

deals.name: ARM Holdings (stake sell-down)
deals.valueNote: FY1999 10-K: $245M in gains from sales of ARM investment recognized in fiscal 1999
deals.description: Apple sold down the ARM stake it had held since co-founding the chip designer with Acorn and VLSI in 1990 — the gains helped fund the turnaround years.
deals.appleLanguage: FY1999 10-K: net income includes $230M+ in gains from sales of the ARM investment.

deals.name: ARM Holdings (further sell-down)
deals.valueNote: FY2000 10-K: $367M gains from investment sales, predominantly ARM
deals.description: Continued sale of the ARM position as the stake wound down through 2003.

deals.name: PowerSchool
deals.valueNote: $62M in Apple stock per Apple's announcement
deals.description: Web-based student information systems — Apple's education-services play; later sold to Pearson in 2006.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple press release, May 2001.

deals.name: Spruce Technologies
deals.description: DVD-authoring software that became DVD Studio Pro.

deals.name: Nothing Real
deals.description: Shake compositing software for film VFX.

deals.name: Emagic
deals.description: German maker of Logic audio software — the foundation of Logic Pro and, later, GarageBand.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple press release, Jul 1, 2002.
deals.source: Apple press release Jul 2002; contemporaneous reporting (~$30M)

deals.name: Fingerworks
deals.description: Multi-touch gesture pioneers — their technology fed directly into the iPhone's touchscreen.

deals.name: Silicon Color
deals.description: Color-grading software that became Apple Color in Final Cut Studio.

deals.name: P.A. Semi
deals.description: The chip-design team that started Apple Silicon: PA Semi's engineers built the A4 and every Apple SoC since — arguably the highest-ROI deal after NeXT.

deals.name: Placebase
deals.description: Mapping platform — an early piece of Apple's break from Google Maps.

deals.name: Lala
deals.valueNote: Price not disclosed; reported ~$17-80M range — no reliable single figure
deals.description: Streaming-music service whose team shaped iTunes Match and iCloud music.

deals.name: Quattro Wireless
deals.description: Mobile advertising network that became iAd.

deals.name: Siri
deals.description: The voice-assistant startup (SRI spin-out) that became Siri, launched with iPhone 4S in 2011 — Apple's first big AI bet.

deals.name: Intrinsity
deals.valueNote: ~$121M, reported by EDN/press at the time
deals.description: Fast-logic chip designers who accelerated the A4 alongside the PA Semi team.

deals.name: Polar Rose
deals.description: Face-recognition technology for Photos.

deals.name: C3 Technologies
deals.valueNote: ~$267M, widely reported (3D mapping spin-out of Saab)
deals.description: 3D mapping — the Flyover views in Apple Maps.

deals.name: Anobit
deals.valueNote: ~$390M, widely reported (Israeli press/Bloomberg); not confirmed by Apple
deals.description: Israeli flash-memory controller firm — Apple's first Israel R&D center grew from it.

deals.name: Chomp
deals.description: App-search engine that improved App Store discovery.

deals.name: AuthenTec
deals.valueNote: $356M — disclosed in the public merger agreement (8-K/proxy)
deals.description: Fingerprint-sensor maker behind Touch ID, announced a year before the iPhone 5s shipped it.
deals.appleLanguage: Merger agreement filed with the SEC: $8.00/share, ~$356M.

deals.name: WifiSLAM
deals.description: Indoor-positioning startup for mapping inside buildings.

deals.name: PrimeSense
deals.description: The 3D-sensing company behind Kinect — its depth-camera technology became Face ID's TrueDepth system.

deals.name: Topsy Labs
deals.description: Twitter-firehose analytics — the team fed search and Siri intelligence.

deals.name: Beats Electronics & Beats Music
deals.description: Apple's largest acquisition ever: Jimmy Iovine and Dr. Dre's headphone brand plus the subscription service that became Apple Music.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple press release, May 28 2014: 'Apple to acquire Beats Music & Beats Electronics… for a total of $3 billion.'

deals.name: FoundationDB
deals.description: Distributed database powering iCloud's backend (later open-sourced).

deals.name: Metaio
deals.description: Augmented-reality pioneer — groundwork for ARKit.

deals.name: Faceshift
deals.description: Real-time facial motion capture — Animoji's ancestry.

deals.name: Emotient
deals.description: Emotion-reading AI from facial expressions.

deals.name: Turi
deals.description: Seattle machine-learning platform; seeded Apple's ML tooling and Create ML.

deals.name: Workflow
deals.description: Automation app that became Shortcuts.

deals.name: Lattice Data
deals.description: Dark-data machine learning (Stanford DeepDive team).

deals.name: Beddit
deals.description: Sleep-tracking hardware and software for Apple Watch's health push.

deals.name: Texture
deals.description: Digital magazine service — became Apple News+.

deals.name: Akonia Holographics
deals.description: Holographic waveguide lenses for AR headsets — Vision Pro groundwork.

deals.name: Shazam
deals.description: Music-recognition service folded into Siri, Music and the OS.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple press release, Sep 24 2018: 'Apple acquires Shazam, offering more ways to discover and enjoy music.'
deals.source: Apple press release Sep 2018; reported price via TechCrunch/FT Dec 2017

deals.name: Platoon
deals.description: Artist-development platform for Apple Music.

deals.name: PullString
deals.description: Voice-app design tools folded into Siri development.

deals.name: Laserlike
deals.description: Machine-learning search startup (ex-Google) for Siri intelligence.

deals.name: Drive.ai
deals.description: Autonomous-driving startup acqui-hired as it wound down — Project Titan talent.

deals.name: Intel smartphone modem business
deals.valueNote: $1.0B — announced jointly by Apple and Intel
deals.description: 2,200 Intel engineers plus patents and equipment — the foundation of Apple's in-house C1 cellular modem shipped in 2025.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple press release, Jul 25 2019: 'Apple to acquire the majority of Intel's smartphone modem business… transaction valued at $1 billion.'

deals.name: Camerai
deals.valueNote: Calcalist reported 'several tens of millions of dollars'; no reliable single figure — left null per accuracy rules
deals.description: Israeli computer-vision/AR startup (formerly Tipit). Deal reportedly occurred ~2019 but was first revealed Aug 2020; team joined Apple's camera/computer-vision group. Exact close date never disclosed.

deals.name: Xnor.ai
deals.valueNote: ~$200M per GeekWire reporting; never confirmed by Apple
deals.description: Seattle edge-AI startup spun out of the Allen Institute for AI (AI2); low-power on-device machine learning that fed into on-device Apple Intelligence-style processing.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.

deals.name: Dark Sky
deals.description: Hyperlocal weather app and API; announced on Dark Sky's own blog Mar 31, 2020. Technology absorbed into Apple's redesigned Weather app; Android app and API shut down.
deals.source: Dark Sky blog announcement, Mar 31 2020; The Verge, Mar 31 2020 (https://www.theverge.com/2020/3/31/21201666/apple-acquires-weather-app-dark-sky-shut-down-android-wear-os-api)

deals.name: Voysis
deals.description: Dublin-based voice/natural-language-understanding platform for improving digital voice assistants; tied to Siri improvements.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.

deals.name: Inductiv
deals.description: Waterloo, Ontario startup using AI to automate identification and correction of errors in datasets; engineering team joined Siri/ML groups.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.

deals.name: NextVR
deals.valueNote: ~$100M per 9to5Mac reporting; Apple confirmed the deal but not the price
deals.description: Live VR sports and concert streaming (NBA, WWE); talent and tech seen as groundwork for Vision Pro immersive video.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.
deals.source: Apple confirmation reported by Bloomberg/9to5Mac, May 14 2020 (https://9to5mac.com/2020/05/14/apple-confirms-nextvr-acquisition/)

deals.name: Fleetsmith
deals.description: San Francisco Apple-device fleet management startup; basis for Apple Business Essentials (launched 2021). One of the rare deals Apple announced openly.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple confirmed the acquisition; Fleetsmith announced 'Fleetsmith is now part of Apple.'

deals.name: Mobeewave
deals.valueNote: ~$100M per Bloomberg reporting; not confirmed by Apple
deals.description: Montreal startup whose NFC tech lets smartphones accept card payments with no extra hardware; became 'Tap to Pay on iPhone' (launched Feb 2022).
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.

deals.name: Spaces
deals.description: VR startup (DreamWorks Animation spin-out) doing location-based VR and VR videoconferencing; relevant to Vision Pro Personas/SharePlay work.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.

deals.name: Scout FM
deals.description: Startup that turned podcasts into curated, hands-free 'radio stations'; tech relevant to Apple Podcasts and CarPlay listening.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.

deals.name: Vilynx
deals.valueNote: ~$50M per Bloomberg reporting; not confirmed by Apple
deals.description: Barcelona AI startup using computer vision to analyze and tag video content; ~50 employees became an Apple AI R&D hub in Barcelona (Siri/search improvements).
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.

deals.name: Curious AI
deals.description: Helsinki-based AI research startup (unsupervised learning / AI simulation); acquisition surfaced Feb 2021 via Finnish press. Exact close date not disclosed.

deals.name: Primephonic
deals.description: Amsterdam classical-music streaming service; one of the few deals Apple announced via a Newsroom press release. Basis for Apple Music Classical (launched Mar 2023).
deals.appleLanguage: Oliver Schusser (Apple VP, Apple Music and Beats): 'We love and have a deep respect for classical music, and Primephonic has become a fan favorite for classical enthusiasts.'

deals.name: AI Music
deals.description: London startup generating personalized, adaptive soundtracks with AI; team folded into Apple's audio/services groups.

deals.name: Credit Kudos
deals.valueNote: ~$150M per The Block reporting; not confirmed by Apple
deals.description: UK open-banking credit-scoring startup; underpinned Apple's UK/EU fintech push and in-house lending ambitions (Apple Pay Later era).
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller technology companies from time to time and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.
deals.source: The Block, Mar 23 2022 (https://www.theblock.co/post/138730/apple-acquires-uk-open-banking-startup-credit-kudos); confirmed by TechCrunch

deals.name: WaveOne
deals.description: Mountain View startup doing AI-powered video compression/codecs; deal reportedly closed quietly ~Jan 2023, revealed Mar 2023 via employee LinkedIn posts.

deals.name: Mira
deals.description: LA-based AR headset maker (US Army and Nintendo theme-park contracts); acquired days after the Vision Pro unveiling; Apple confirmed with its standard statement.
deals.appleLanguage: Apple buys smaller companies from time to time, and we generally do not discuss our purpose or plans.

deals.name: BIS Records
deals.description: Swedish classical label founded 1973; joined Apple Music Classical/Platoon arm. Announced by BIS founder Robert von Bahr, Sep 2023 — Apple's first record-label purchase.
deals.source: BIS Records announcement via Gramophone/9to5Mac, Sep 2023 (https://9to5mac.com/2023/09/14/apple-acquires-classical-music-label/)

deals.name: Datakalab
deals.description: Paris startup specializing in AI compression and on-device computer vision. Deal signed Dec 17 2023 but only revealed Apr 2024 by French press — relevant to on-device Apple Intelligence.

deals.name: DarwinAI
deals.description: Canadian AI startup for visual quality inspection in manufacturing and making AI models smaller/faster; dozens of employees joined Apple's AI group pre-Apple Intelligence launch.

deals.name: Mayday Labs
deals.description: Canadian maker of the AI calendar/task app Mayday. Acquired Apr 2024; disclosed only via an EU Digital Markets Act filing published Aug 2024.

deals.name: Pixelmator
deals.description: Vilnius-based maker of Pixelmator Pro and Photomator. Announced Nov 1 2024 by the Pixelmator team; per Apple's EU DMA filing the deal closed Feb 11 2025 after regulatory clearance.
deals.appleLanguage: Pixelmator team: 'Today we have some important news to share: the Pixelmator Team plans to join Apple.'
deals.source: Pixelmator announcement, Nov 1 2024 (https://www.pixelmator.com/blog/2024/11/01/a-new-home-for-pixelmator/); close date per EU DMA filing via 9to5Mac, Feb 11 2026 (https://9to5mac.com/2026/02/11/kuzu-database-company-joins-apples-list-of-recent-acquisitions/)

deals.name: Pointable
deals.description: Developed enterprise-grade natural-language retrieval systems for building custom LLM applications. Close date per Apple's EU Digital Markets Act disclosure.

deals.name: TrueMeeting
deals.description: Founded as CommonGround-AI; smartphone face-scan avatars for video chat. First reported by Bloomberg in 2024 but Apple's EU DMA filing records the close as Jan 24 2025 (dashboard uses filing date; some trackers list it under 2024).
deals.source: EU DMA filing via 9to5Mac, Feb 11 2026; earlier reporting Road to VR/Bloomberg 2024 (https://www.roadtovr.com/apple-acquires-truemeeting-avatars-vision-pro/)

deals.name: WhyLabs
deals.description: Seattle startup (founded 2019, ex-Amazon ML team) for monitoring and analyzing ML models and data pipelines; founders joined Apple AI roles. Surfaced via GeekWire sleuthing, confirmed by EU DMA filing.
deals.source: GeekWire, 2025 (https://www.geekwire.com/2025/did-apple-just-buy-another-seattle-startup-clues-point-to-secretive-acquisition/); EU DMA filing via 9to5Mac, Feb 11 2026

deals.name: IC Mask Design
deals.description: Irish firm providing physical layout design services for analog integrated circuits plus training; supports Apple silicon effort. Close date per EU DMA filing.
deals.source: AppleInsider, Jul 7 2025 (https://appleinsider.com/articles/25/07/07/apple-buys-two-eu-firms-to-improve-apple-intelligence-apple-vision-pro); EU DMA filing via 9to5Mac, Feb 11 2026

deals.name: Styra
deals.category: Cloud infrastructure security (authorization / Open Policy Agent)
deals.description: Creator-company of Open Policy Agent; develops and licenses authorization software for cloud-native environments — relevant to Private Cloud Compute. Close date per EU DMA filing.

deals.name: Prompt AI (talent + technology)
deals.valueNote: Price not disclosed; structured as talent-and-technology purchase, not full-company acquisition
deals.description: 11-person computer-vision startup co-founded by Berkeley's Tete Xiao and Trevor Darrell (maker of Seemour app); Apple acquired the team and software assets, beating interest from xAI/Neuralink, per CNBC.

deals.name: invrs.io LLC
deals.description: Tiny AI-guided technology company; sole employee hired by Apple. Revealed Feb 2026 via regulatory disclosure; thinly sourced — flagged as low-detail in notes.
deals.source: MacRumors Apple acquisition guide, retrieved Aug 16 2026 (https://www.macrumors.com/guide/apple-acquisition/)

deals.name: Kuzu
deals.description: Ontario-based (Univ. of Waterloo spin-out, ~10 employees) lightweight embedded graph-database technology; potential fit for on-device Apple Intelligence knowledge retrieval. Close date per EU DMA filing.
deals.source: EU DMA filing via 9to5Mac, Feb 11 2026; The Mac Observer (https://www.macobserver.com/news/apple-buys-graph-database-startup-kuzu-eu-filing-shows-more/)

deals.name: PlasmaSolve
deals.valueNote: Price not disclosed; exact close date not stated in DMA summary
deals.description: Czech (Brno) plasma-physics simulation firm (founded 2016); MatSight software simulates plasma processes such as ultra-thin coatings on 3D device surfaces — relevant to future iPhone/Watch/Mac materials and finishes. Revealed via EU DMA filing, reported Aug 3 2026.

deals.name: Q.ai
deals.valueNote: 'Close to $2B' per The Information/MacRumors; Israeli press (Ynet/Jerusalem Post) reported $1.5–1.6B; Apple has not disclosed the price. Second-largest Apple acquisition ever after Beats ($3B, 2014).
deals.description: Secretive ~100-person Israeli startup whose AI reads facial micro-movements and subtle audio to interpret 'silent speech' — enabling non-verbal Siri interaction and wearables input. Founders include PrimeSense co-founder Aviad Maizels (PrimeSense became Face ID). Completed January 2026.
deals.appleLanguage: Johny Srouji (SVP Hardware Technologies): 'a remarkable company that is pioneering new and creative ways to use imaging and machine learning… excited for what's to come.'
deals.source: MacRumors, Feb 3 2026 and Jul 29 2026 (https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/29/apple-second-biggest-acquisition-this-year/); The Information via MacRumors, Jul 15 2026; Ynet (https://www.ynetnews.com/tech-and-digital/article/hyvyzdql11e)

deals.name: Color.io (Patchflyer GmbH)
deals.valueNote: Price not disclosed; assets and key personnel
deals.description: Web-based color-grading tool for photographers and filmmakers; Apple acquired the technology and key personnel. Revealed via EU DMA regulatory filing.
deals.source: EU DMA filing via MacRumors Apple acquisition guide, retrieved Aug 16 2026 (https://www.macrumors.com/guide/apple-acquisition/)

deals.name: Animato
deals.valueNote: Price not disclosed; structured acqui-hire (employment offers + non-exclusive IP license + patent applications)
deals.description: Virtual-avatar software for video chats and tutoring. Filed under the EU DMA in Jan 2026 as a structured acqui-hire; reported May 19 2026.

deals.name: Play
deals.description: Award-winning Mac/iPhone app-design tool (Apple Design Award winner) letting designers build native iOS interfaces and hand off to SwiftUI. Closed Feb 2026 per EU filing; reported June 2026.
deals.source: EU DMA filing via MacRumors Apple acquisition guide / 9to5Mac reporting, Jun 2026 (https://www.macrumors.com/guide/apple-acquisition/)

deals.name: SigScalr (assets + team)
deals.valueNote: Price not disclosed; partial acquisition of assets and engineering talent per EU DMA database
deals.description: Maker of open-source SigLens observability platform (logs, metrics, traces at scale). Notified to the EU Mar 12 2026 under the DMA; surfaced publicly Jul 13 2026. Supports Apple's internal services/AI infrastructure tooling.
deals.source: EU DMA filing via 9to5Mac, Jul 13 2026 (https://9to5mac.com/2026/07/13/apple-acquires-observability-startup-sigscalr/); MacRumors, Jul 13 2026 (https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/13/apple-acquires-sigscalr-assets/)

notes: Interim list: 2020-2026 fully researched (36 deals, sources per deal incl. EU DMA filings); pre-2020 curated from the well-documented public record — to be replaced by the full researched sweep. SCOPE & METHOD: Covers all publicly known Apple acquisitions Jan 2020 – Aug 16 2026. Apple almost never discloses prices; every valueMillions figure is press-reported (source cited per deal), not Apple-confirmed — treat as 'reported'. Undisclosed = null. No divestitures: Apple made no material divestitures in this period. Many 2024–2026 deals only became public because Apple, as an EU Digital Mark
